newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate falls on reserve cut rumour.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate falls on reserve cut rumour.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to as low as 6.0 percent on Wednesday, triggered by rumours that the statutory reserve requirement (SRR) may be cut due to the current tight liquidity situation, dealers said.
"There's a strong rumour of an SRR cut which pulled the overnight all the way down to 6.0 percent from about 8.0 percent," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
The overnight closed at 8.30/40 percent on Tuesday.
But dealers said it was hard to believe that Bank Negara would take such an action.

The central bank last raised the SRR -- funds that must be placed interest free with the central bank -- to 12.5 percent of a financial institution's total liabilities on February 1, 1996 from 11.5 percent.

"Theoratically, a cut would release funds into the system and this may be a reason for the rumour. But we doubt this is an avenue Bank Negara will take as it would send a wrong signal to the market, what with monetary and consumption growth still high," said research house MMS International in its market commentary.
A better alternative to add liquidity would be to let Bank Negara bills mature without roll-overs, it said.
Dealers said the fall in the overnight could exert further pressure on interbank rates on Thursday.
Earlier, one- and two-week money were at 7.80/8.30 percent against 8.50/60 percent on Tuesday.
One-month money was at 8.10/20 percent from 8.40/50, and three-month at 8.00/10 percent against 8.00/20.
A large local bank was seen lending one-month money this morning, prompting the belief that Bank Negara may have stepped in to provide liquidity to ease the squeeze.
"I think Bank Negara is injecting funds to help ease the market. Rates have remained high for about a month due to a liquidity squeeze," said one dealer.
Dealers said foreign banks, which had some excess funds, were among the lenders this morning.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange rose sharply across the board as investors turned buyers following a sudden easing of interbank rates, futures dealers said.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up 17 points to 92.15, or an implied yield of 7.85 percent.
The September contract was up 15 at 92.46, or 7.54 percent, and December was up 11 at 92.56, or 7.44 percent,
